currentContext.business: Ram Ratna Wires, operating since 1992, manufactures copper and aluminium winding wires and strips across one of the industry's widest dimensional ranges (from 5 mm down to ultra-fine 0.016 mm), serving India's electrical ecosystem. It has expanded beyond winding wires into specialised conductors, value-added electrical solutions and seamless copper tubes (via the Bhiwadi facility and merged Global Copper), positioning itself as an integrated copper products platform. It supplies leading OEMs across automotive, industrial, HVAC and electronics, with OEM customers driving roughly 70-75% of business.

Winding wires & strips: Fiber glass covered copper and aluminium strips
Parallel wires for EV hub motor windings

currentContext.strengths: India's leading manufacturer of winding wires and strips; among India's largest copper tube manufacturing operations|Ability to manufacture across one of the widest dimensional ranges in the industry (5 mm to 0.016 mm), a capability among limited organised players in India|Preferred supplier to leading OEMs (Cummins, Siemens, CG Power, Schneider Electric, Havells, Godrej & Boyce, Amber Enterprises, Epack Durables, Daikin, Panasonic Life Solutions, Bosch), driving ~70-75% of business|Robust pan-India distribution network|Diversified portfolio across many product lines so strength is not tied to a single product or plant|Vertically integrated, technology-driven manufacturing with automation, integrated quality monitoring and Eddy Current Testing|Copper tubes localisation / import-substitution positioning in a segment historically dependent on imports
currentContext.strategies: Reinvestment-led: the Company funds capacity expansion (new Bhiwadi copper-tube facility under the PLI scheme, taking it to five manufacturing plants) and its green-energy portfolio (raising its stake in subsidiary Tefabo Product Pvt. Ltd. to 64%). Members approved enhancing the Section 180(1)(c) borrowing limit to Rs 1,500 crores (from Rs 1,200 crores) to support business needs, with corresponding enhancement of the Section 180(1)(a) charge-creation limit. The Company accepts no public deposits, and unclaimed dividends/shares are transferred to the IEPF per statute. No buyback, sweat-equity or differential-rights issuance during the year.|Resource efficiency: implement lean manufacturing and invest in advanced machinery to minimise waste and process scrap, reducing copper/raw-material consumption|Energy and emissions: adopt renewable energy, replace inefficient machines, conduct regular energy audits, and use catalytic enamelling machines to minimise emissions|Occupational health and safety: mandatory safety training, regular drills, ISO 45001 certification processes, and incident-reporting systems|Vendor ESG: transition from standard contractual purchase-order clauses to a structured vendor ESG assessment framework with verification mechanisms|Value-added product portfolio: increase R&D investment and technology-transfer partnerships to shift toward higher-margin, innovation-led products (e.g., paper magnet wires, ultrafine copper wires)|Regulatory compliance: deploy robust compliance monitoring systems, regular legal audits, and active engagement with regulatory bodies
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26 Ram Ratna Wires pursued inorganic expansion and structural consolidation; the routed capex sections disclose no greenfield plant/line capacity-addition project with a commissioning timeline. The NCLT (Mumbai Bench) sanctioned the merger by absorption of Global Copper Private Limited - described as a material unlisted subsidiary - into the Company (order dated May 29, 2025; Scheme effective June 23, 2025 on filing with the RoC; appointed date April 01, 2024), integrating the copper business into the parent. The Company completed acquisition of an additional 4% stake in its subsidiary Tefabo Product Private Limited (registered office in Bangalore), raising its holding from 60% to 64%. It retains two joint venture companies - Epavo Electricals Private Limited (Maharashtra) and RR-Imperial Electricals Limited (based in Bangladesh). To support future funding needs, members were asked (Special Resolution at the AGM) to enhance the Section 180(1)(c) borrowing limit from Rs 1,200 crores to Rs 1,500 crores. Capital-structure actions during the year included a 1:1 bonus issue and an increase in authorized share capital from Rs 25 crores to Rs 50 crores.

risks.risk: Copper raw-material intensity and price volatility
risks.note: Efficient use of raw materials, particularly copper, is critical for the resource-intensive winding-wire and copper-tube operations; inefficient consumption directly erodes margins and strains supply resilience.
Energy consumption remains a major driver of manufacturing costs, and efficiency investments are needed to stay aligned with evolving environmental regulations and climate commitments.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in manufacturing
risks.note: Manufacturing operations inherently carry workplace risks; strong safety systems are essential for workforce protection and statutory compliance, with failures risking legal and financial penalties.

The supply chain is a significant source of indirect environmental and social impact; vendor failure to adhere to ESG standards can cause supply disruptions, reputational damage, and financial penalties.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance across environmental, labour and corporate rules
risks.note: Operations are subject to varied environmental, labour and corporate regulations; lapses can cause business disruptions and fines, requiring proactive compliance monitoring.

Exposure to demand fluctuations and geographic-sector concentration; the Company pursues market diversification across geographies and sectors (EV, renewable energy) and export expansion to reduce this risk.

risks.risk: Commoditisation and margin pressure in standard products
risks.note: Reliance on commoditised wire products invites competitive pressure; a strategic shift toward higher-margin value-added products (paper magnet wires, ultrafine copper wires) is being pursued to defend profitability.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.
